data.title: Treasurer & CFO Brandon Filson Sold A Bunch Of Shares In Angel Oak Mortgage REIT
data.description:
We wouldn't blame Angel Oak Mortgage REIT, Inc. (NYSE:AOMR) shareholders if they were a little worried about the fact that Brandon Filson, the Treasurer & CFO recently netted about US$515k selling shares at an average price of US$7.93. That sale reduced their total holding by 38% which is hardly insignificant, but far from the worst we've seen.

In fact, the recent sale by Brandon Filson was the biggest sale of Angel Oak Mortgage REIT shares made by an insider individual in the last twelve months, according to our records. So what is clear is that an insider saw fit to sell at around the current price of US$7.55. While insider selling is a negative, to us, it is more negative if the shares are sold at a lower price. We note that this sale took place at around the current price, so it isn't a major concern, though it's hardly a good sign.

Based on our data, Angel Oak Mortgage REIT insiders have about 2.3% of the stock, worth approximately US$4.0m. We consider this fairly low insider ownership.

The insider sales have outweighed the insider buying, at Angel Oak Mortgage REIT, in the last three months. Zooming out, the longer term picture doesn't give us much comfort. data.title: Here's Why We're Not Too Worried About Terra Rossa Gold's (CVE:TRR) Cash Burn Situation
data.description:
Even when a business is losing money, it's possible for shareholders to make money if they buy a good business at the right price. For example, although software-as-a-service business Salesforce.com lost money for years while it grew recurring revenue, if you held shares since 2005, you'd have done very well indeed. But the harsh reality is that very many loss making companies burn through all their cash and go bankrupt.

Given this risk, we thought we'd take a look at whether Terra Rossa Gold (CVE:TRR) shareholders should be worried about its cash burn. In this article, we define cash burn as its annual (negative) free cash flow, which is the amount of money a company spends each year to fund its growth. Let's start with an examination of the business' cash, relative to its cash burn.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

When Might Terra Rossa Gold Run Out Of Money?

You can calculate a company's cash runway by dividing the amount of cash it has by the rate at which it is spending that cash. In June 2026, Terra Rossa Gold had CA$5.3m in cash, and was debt-free. Looking at the last year, the company burnt through CA$1.5m. That means it had a cash runway of about 3.6 years as of June 2026. A runway of this length affords the company the time and space it needs to develop the business. You can see how its cash balance has changed over time in the image below.

View our latest analysis for Terra Rossa Gold

How Is Terra Rossa Gold's Cash Burn Changing Over Time?

Because Terra Rossa Gold isn't currently generating revenue, we consider it an early-stage business. Nonetheless, we can still examine its cash burn trajectory as part of our assessment of its cash burn situation. During the last twelve months, its cash burn actually ramped up 61%. Oftentimes, increased cash burn simply means a company is accelerating its business development, but one should always be mindful that this causes the cash runway to shrink. Admittedly, we're a bit cautious of Terra Rossa Gold due to its lack of significant operating revenues. So we'd generally prefer stocks from this list of stocks that have analysts forecasting growth.

How Easily Can Terra Rossa Gold Raise Cash?

While Terra Rossa Gold does have a solid cash runway, its cash burn trajectory may have some shareholders thinking ahead to when the company may need to raise more cash. Generally speaking, a listed business can raise new cash through issuing shares or taking on debt. Many companies end up issuing new shares to fund future growth. We can compare a company's cash burn to its market capitalisation to get a sense for how many new shares a company would have to issue to fund one year's operations.

Since it has a market capitalisation of CA$29m, Terra Rossa Gold's CA$1.5m in cash burn equates to about 5.1% of its market value. Given that is a rather small percentage, it would probably be really easy for the company to fund another year's growth by issuing some new shares to investors, or even by taking out a loan.

Is Terra Rossa Gold's Cash Burn A Worry?

It may already be apparent to you that we're relatively comfortable with the way Terra Rossa Gold is burning through its cash. For example, we think its cash runway suggests that the company is on a good path. While its increasing cash burn wasn't great, the other factors mentioned in this article more than make up for weakness on that measure. Looking at all the measures in this article, together, we're not worried about its rate of cash burn; the company seems well on top of its medium-term spending needs.
